components.text: STEP 12 has Chinese data at BMI 24 to <28, the Wegovy label is unchanged

footnote: Source: Novo Nordisk, Lilly and Huadong announcements, mazdutide label, national weight management guidance (2024), STEP 12 (2026)
notes: There are two sets of label thresholds, so prescriptions must be checked against the label of the drug prescribed. Wegovy and liraglutide 3.0 mg follow the international standard: a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 to 30 with at least one weight-related comorbidity. Tirzepatide and mazdutide follow the Chinese standard: 28 or more, or 24 or more with at least one comorbidity, the same cut-offs as China's 2024 weight management guidance. That guidance also says patients with obesity should first try 3 to 6 months of lifestyle change and move to drugs if they lose less than 5%. Wegovy's cardiovascular indication is separate: established cardiovascular disease and a BMI of at least 27. A note on STEP 12: it studied Chinese adults with a BMI of 24 to 28, who lost 12.1%, but we found no approval moving Wegovy's Chinese label to 28/24. Prescribing Wegovy at those levels is therefore off-label and needs informed consent and a filing. We could not find the official BMI threshold for ecnoglutide.
